### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **39** documentable anchor(s).

**36** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e40cd1e28dd79e60e7f4be0db06f071f3f962574`.

⛔ **15** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `/meta/:type/:name (route, 48 pages)`
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e40cd1e28dd79e60e7f4be0db06f071f3f962574` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fd04e4b7fbb4da7048b3f0ec2955ea834760171e` — the merge of head `8d85d2b1afb2d6e89d6c28ee0f3aa64c9b427585` into base `e40cd1e28dd79e60e7f4be0db06f071f3f962574`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin fd04e4b7fbb4da7048b3f0ec2955ea834760171e && git checkout fd04e4b7fbb4da7048b3f0ec2955ea834760171e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e40cd1e28dd79e60e7f4be0db06f071f3f962574 8d85d2b1afb2d6e89d6c28ee0f3aa64c9b427585 && git checkout -B drift-repro e40cd1e28dd79e60e7f4be0db06f071f3f962574 && git merge --no-ff 8d85d2b1afb2d6e89d6c28ee0f3aa64c9b427585

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e40cd1e28dd79e60e7f4be0db06f071f3f962574
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e40cd1e28dd79e60e7f4be0db06f071f3f962574` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8d85d2b1afb2d6e89d6c28ee0f3aa64c9b427585`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.stored-row-own-package-slot.ts + packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-registry-hydration.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-exact-qualifier.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-face.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-reads.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.register-item-call-sites.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/protocol-cluster-signal-package.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/protocol-flow-custom-override.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/webhook-stored-row-boot-hydration.test.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-disabled-holder-served-stack.test.ts, scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json, .changeset/33127-stored-row-own-package-slot.md, .changeset/33127-stored-row-own-package-slot-semantic-entry.md (read, not reviewed: registry readers that walk raw keys — bareNamePackageHolders, securityCatalog*, listItems; plugin-webhooks declared-webhooks.ts slotsOf; runtime action-execution.ts listItems consumers)

Face: schema (a `packages/spec/src/**` hit). Diff read against merge base `e0ce1b52`. Cards #32900, #32663, #32662, #33127 and #33131 (with every comment) read.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Slot model.** A stored row of a package-slotted type (`PACKAGE_SLOTTED_STORE_TYPES` minus `flow` and `permission`) that is bound to a package now registers under `NUL pkg NUL bareKey` (`registerItem`'s `storedRowPackage`). A package-less row keeps the bare slot, and code artifacts keep `pkg:name`. Raw-key readers outside the PR were checked against the new key form. `bundleBaseKey`, `bareNamePackageHolders`, the security-catalog scans and the `:name` suffix scans neither match an overlay key nor count it as a holder (no `:` in it, never equal to a bare name), as the `OVERLAY_SLOT_MARK` docblock claims.
- **Readers moved with it.** `bareSlotEntriesOf` appends the overlay slots, so `getPackageScopedItem`, holders and `overlaySlotBinding` see every stored row. `getItem` reads bare, then overlays (`orderedOverlayTier`: the caller's package first, then composite-holder order, then id), then composites. That is the same precedence the bare slot had over composites, now independent of registration order. `rankedForPackage` mirrors `servedOverlayRowCandidates`' order (declared override of the pair, own row, package-less, other bound). `boundServedActions` lets one overlay per (holder, name) shadow that holder's composite, as the bare slot shadows every composite. `unregisterItem` removes one package's overlay group before falling to composites, and `removePackageOverlaySlots` retires only the removed row's package slot.
- **Hydration and heal.** `hydrateOverlayIntoRegistry` passes `storedRowPackage` only for the slotted types. The sole-holder envelope record is skipped for overlay-slot keys, which is correct because the bare key is untouched. The delete heal retires the bound slot and leaves the package-less bare row alone. A peer with an unknown binding retires every slot that no remaining row is bound to.
- **Protocol reads.** `admitExactQualifier`'s `storedRowBases` admits a pair address at the one base whose stored row holds the name. Two such bases are refused by `exactQualifierItem` as two registry bases are. It is asked only by the plain item read. `storedRowHoldersRefusal` serves the one holder whose rows are its own plus its pair's (scope note (b)).
- **Downstream consumers.** `listItems(type)` now yields one row per bound package where it used to yield the last one. plugin-webhooks resolves slots through `getPackageScopedItem` / `packageScopedHoldersOf` (`slotsOf`), and runtime's `listItems('action')` consumers filter by `_packageId` stamps that the rows already wore. Neither keys on the bare slot, so neither double-counts.
- **Pins.** The `#33131 S1` "(carried)" pin is flipped: each holder's registry item is now its own override, in 2 × 2 orders. Webhook, tool, agent and skill boot cover 2 holders in every registration and row order, with CONTROLs (one row, one holder). #32900 covers both row orders plus CONTROLs. There is also a cluster-signal peer pin and REST served-stack pins. `engine-double-contract.pinned.json` goes 2 → 4, which grows the pinned population and loosens nothing.
- **CI** on this head at review time: 23 success, 13 skipped, 31 in progress. `PR-body guards` had FAILED, which the author attributes to the folded cards' claim comments and has re-patched. Landing needs every check green on the landing head.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is right. The diff widens `@objectstack/objectql`'s exported `SchemaRegistry` (an optional fifth `registerItem` argument and the public `removePackageOverlaySlots`) and narrows one answer: an action two packages hold only as stored rows, read with no package after a restart, goes from 200 (the last hydrated) to 409 naming both, matching #32607. A diff that widens and narrows takes `yes (narrowing)` (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3). `Metadata-protocol: semantic` is right, because which stored row each package's address serves changes and no key moves. `@objectstack/objectql` and `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` are `minor`, `@objectstack/spec` is `patch` (`none`), and `adr-0087: registered stored-row-own-package-slot`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Not governed (no Tier H path); 737 lines, under the 3000-line bound. The PR is authored by `objectstack-fleet[bot]` on the relay.
- N1 (nit, performance): for a non-bundle type, `getItem` (bare miss) and `bareSlotEntriesOf` now walk the whole collection (`overlaySlotEntriesOf`) where they used to answer from one `Map.get`. The callers are metadata reads, not per-record paths, so this is bounded. A per-type count of overlay keys, skipping the walk at zero (the common case), would restore O(1).
- N2 (nit): `getItem(name)` with no package and two packages' overlay rows now picks by composite-holder order instead of save order. Internal callers that use it as a baseline (`protocol-save.ts` baseline, the authoring gate's declared body) get a deterministic but still arbitrary pick. That is no worse than before, since the doors themselves refuse 409, but a short comment at those two callers would keep a later reader from relying on it.
- N3 (nit): `boundServedActions` splits its group key on the last `:`. Safe for action names today; a tuple key would not depend on it.

### ④ Design judgment

`18.stored-row-own-package-slot.ts` holds against ADR-0150 D3/D4 ("registry overlay slot (ADR-0005)": a stored row bound to a package is that package's item) and red line 2. Its `surface`, `replacement` and `acceptanceCriteria` name every moved read, including the peer replica and the pair address, and give the operator's remedy (`?package=ID`). The registry change agrees with it: the one-bare-slot model was the root of every order-dependence named in #33127, #32663, #32662, #32900 and the #33131 carried face, and each now has a pin in both orders. The exclusions (`flow`, which keeps #28717's declared-override slot rule, and `permission`, which keeps its fork ruling) are reasoned in `takesPackageOverlaySlot`. No must-fix or should-fix; N1–N3 are nits. This is the final round.

**#33131 (asked by the author):** this PR closes that card's remaining **carried** face (comment 6870666736, the both-overridden registry item), and the flipped pin proves it. Two items are still open on the card (comment 6878816309): nit N1 of record 6878787461 (unmeasured), and the `doc` bare-read registration-order pick, which is out of this PR's types. So this PR alone does not finish #33131. Keep `Refs #33131`, or file one loose-ends card carrying those two items, link it on #33131, and then write `Fixes #33131`.
